title: DNS from both sides
scenario: "Marketing will announce portal.edymonte.com.br next week. Confirm the domain is served by our Azure DNS and that internal names resolve privately." — Product owner
mission: Verify public delegation and private resolution, and explain the difference.
objectives: Verify NS delegation from the registrar
Inspect private DNS records created by private endpoints

prerequisites.notes: Delegation submitted at the registrar (done in day 1).

steps.title: Public delegation
steps.detail: Ask a public resolver for the NS of the domain.

steps.title: Private records
steps.detail: List A records in both privatelink zones.
steps.command: az network private-dns record-set a list -g rg-mfs-hub-lab -z privatelink.database.windows.net -o table

steps.title: Explain
steps.detail: Why does the same SQL name resolve to different IPs from your laptop and from a pod?

criteria.text: Public resolvers return the Azure DNS name servers for the domain
Each privatelink zone has an A record for its private endpoint

expectedResult: Public DNS owned by Azure DNS; private names answered by linked private zones.
recovery: If NS still show the registrar, propagation is pending or DNSSEC is enabled at the registrar.
dont: Do not create public records by hand — every record is Terraform
hints: Delegation is a set of NS records at the parent zone (.br).
Private endpoint DNS zone groups create the A records for you.
From inside the VNet the privatelink zone answers; from outside the public zone does.

interview.question: A pod resolves the SQL server to a public IP and times out. What happened?
followUps: Why does the public DNS zone live in the bootstrap layer?

debrief: Split-horizon: the public chain ends in a firewalled public IP; inside linked VNets, the privatelink zone answers with the private IP. A missing VNet link makes pods resolve the public IP → timeout (game day GD-04).

checker.plan: Read-only: DNS NS query against a public resolver, az network private-dns record-set a list for both zones.
